current: current contracts, manifests and safe contract tests

gokv_oci_dool.reason: This mission consolidates verified documentation and does not promote a new learning item.

required_truths: Current authority and published Git checkpoint are coherent.
Every 3.x terrain surface has provenance, owner boundary, dependency and exit relevance.
The 36-route legacy surface has a documented security, ownership, destination and retirement decision.
Canonical permission, request, confirmation, activation and response contracts have an explicit route coverage decision.
Legacy provider, secret and mutation paths are either isolated, retired or connected through an approved canonical boundary.
Persistence, lifecycle, materialization and rollback destinations are explicit and testable.
Agent, preset, paper and team activation states are distinct from source definitions and runtime authority.
All required safe tests and historical guards pass against their own checkpoints.
No forbidden product, runtime, deployment or external-evidence unknown is being treated as closed by assumption.
required_security_truths: HTTP identity, authentication, authorization, ownership and tenant scope are explicit.
CORS and trust-boundary policy is an approved decision, not a source default.
Secret input, storage, redaction, rotation and exposure semantics are explicit.
Legacy route mutation and provider paths have a fail-closed boundary.
required_contract_truths: Request envelopes, permission decisions, capability policy and confirmation semantics agree.
Payload and response contracts are versioned and route ownership is explicit.
Contract existence is not mistaken for route coverage.
required_lifecycle_truths: Attempt, execution, active-contract, executor, approval and rollback states are separated.
Sandbox materialization cannot be confused with operational writes.
Lifecycle terminal states and recovery ownership are testable.
required_provider_truths: Provider reachability, credentials, network effects and runtime activation are separately evidenced.
No source-callable provider path is treated as deployed or active without allowed evidence.
required_persistence_truths: Every write-capable path has an explicit destination, owner, retention and rollback policy.
Memory, evidence, product stores and sandbox artifacts are separated.
required_legacy_truths: Legacy API routes have an approved coverage, bridge, retirement or containment decision.
No implicit legacy-to-canonical authority is assumed.
required_test_truths: Focal, group, canonical and deep historical suites are selected by risk.
Historical guards validate their own published interval.
Negative evidence and forbidden states remain asserted.
allowed_unknowns_at_3x_exit: Future sector-specific enterprise requirements outside the approved phase.
Future product features explicitly classified as architectural reservations.
External evidence intentionally deferred to a separately authorized operational phase.
forbidden_unknowns_at_3x_exit: Unclassified legacy mutation or provider route coverage.
Unowned secret or persistence write destination.
Implicit authority granted by source presence or a plan label.
Deployment or runtime claims without evidence.
A phase exit claim based only on document existence.

blocks.objective: Fix authority and define the 3.x completion contract.
blocks.why_now_or_when: Entry block for every future 3.x route.
blocks.test_policy: focal continuity and documentary guards; no product imports
blocks.rollback_model: revert only this documentary station if authority mismatch appears
postconditions: exit truths and forbidden unknowns explicit

blocks.objective: Resolve the legacy exposure and trust boundary.
blocks.why_now_or_when: Before any bridge, remediation or activation decision.
blocks.test_policy: static route guards plus explicitly authorized external-evidence branch; no secrets or provider calls by default
blocks.rollback_model: preserve audit docs and revert only the current station artifacts
postconditions: exposure, identity, CORS, secret and deployment unknowns are classified

blocks.objective: Decide how legacy routes relate to the canonical control plane.
blocks.why_now_or_when: After trust boundary evidence, before route remediation.
blocks.test_policy: contract provenance and negative bridge checks; no bridge implementation in documentary phase
blocks.rollback_model: revert route decision documentation only; preserve B-1 evidence
postconditions: every route has covered, contained, retired or explicitly deferred destination

blocks.objective: Reconcile request, permission, confirmation, payload and lifecycle contracts.
blocks.why_now_or_when: After the destination decision makes contract gaps concrete.
blocks.test_policy: focal contract tests, canonical safe suites, no endpoint execution
blocks.rollback_model: revert only contract documentation/test station; no product change
postconditions: no contract exists without an owner and route decision

blocks.objective: Resolve activation, runtime, provider and network readiness boundaries.
blocks.why_now_or_when: Only after request and permission semantics are stable.
blocks.test_policy: static and contract tests first; runtime/provider tests require separate authorization
blocks.rollback_model: stop before runtime edge; revert only documentary readiness station
postconditions: no runtime/provider capability is inferred from source presence

blocks.objective: Close persistence, sandbox, lifecycle and rollback ownership.
blocks.why_now_or_when: Can proceed in parallel with B-4 once B-3 gives destinations.
blocks.test_policy: static path guards and sandbox contract suites; no operational writes
blocks.rollback_model: station-local documentary rollback; sandbox fixtures only when safe
postconditions: product, evidence and sandbox stores are separated

blocks.objective: Reconcile agent, preset, paper and team readiness without fake activation.
blocks.why_now_or_when: After permission, activation and storage boundaries are explicit.
blocks.test_policy: definitions and contract tests only; no agent execution or provider calls
blocks.rollback_model: revert readiness docs/tests only; preserve non-operational source
postconditions: source definitions are not called active workforce

blocks.objective: Assemble evidence and determine whether ROADMAP_3_X_CLOSED is true.
blocks.why_now_or_when: Terminal block after all blocking surfaces have decisions and evidence.
input_postconditions: B-0 through B-6 complete or explicitly allowed unknown
blocks.test_policy: focal -> group -> canonical -> deep historical according to risk
blocks.rollback_model: if exit condition fails, preserve green block commits and return to the named unmet block
postconditions: next phase entry contract is explicit

continue_if: route exposure and identity questions are classified
recalculate_if: new route or owner surface is discovered
stop_if: policy decision is required before evidence exists
reorder_if: same 3.x destination and B-2 evidence can be gathered earlier
human_decision_if: trust, tenant or ownership semantics change

continue_if: permission and activation boundaries remain explicit
stop_if: runtime or provider activation is requested without authority

continue_if: write destinations are sandbox or explicitly governed
recalculate_if: new store or lifecycle owner appears
reorder_if: same phase destination; persistence evidence is a demonstrated precondition for B-4

continue_if: activation readiness remains contract-only or separately authorized
recalculate_if: agent/team definitions are found to have active authority
stop_if: agent execution or provider calls are proposed

continue_if: sandbox and operational storage remain distinct

frontiers.why_sensitive: Historical guard scope can misclassify later missions.
dissolve_if: guard compares its own historical interval
apparent_if: failure appears only from later legitimate files
frontiers.reconnaissance_branch: inspect baseline, final checkpoint and diff semantics
frontiers.route_recalculation_trigger: later mission artifacts appear in old allowlist failure

frontiers.why_sensitive: Route exposure and identity are not proven by source registration.
dissolve_if: approved read-only deployment evidence is available
apparent_if: repository lacks hosting metadata but deployment is known
frontiers.route_recalculation_trigger: edge evidence changes route exposure classification

frontiers.why_sensitive: CORS trust is an architectural policy, not a code-only observation.
dissolve_if: Direction approves a trust policy and evidence path
apparent_if: wildcard is an inert local-only configuration
frontiers.route_recalculation_trigger: deployment edge proves a narrower effective policy

frontiers.why_sensitive: api_key and config writes cross secret and persistence boundaries.
dissolve_if: existing secret and storage contracts cover the route
apparent_if: write path is unreachable behind a separate verified edge
true_hard_if: new secret storage or ownership policy is needed
frontiers.safe_pause_condition: secret values or live stores would be required

frontiers.why_sensitive: Legacy routes need a single authority destination.
dissolve_if: Direction chooses bridge, containment or retirement
apparent_if: existing internal contracts already define the destination
true_hard_if: a new authority or product boundary is required
frontiers.safe_pause_condition: bridge or retirement policy is undecided
frontiers.route_recalculation_trigger: new route family or owner is discovered

frontiers.why_sensitive: Internal contracts exist but route use is not demonstrated.
dissolve_if: static adapter evidence proves current contract coverage
apparent_if: same contract is used through an indirect symbol
true_hard_if: adapter changes authority or payload semantics
frontiers.safe_pause_condition: indirect call path cannot be proven safely
frontiers.route_recalculation_trigger: canonical entrypoint is found or ruled out

frontiers.why_sensitive: Activation gates can be mistaken for active runtime authority.
dissolve_if: all transitions remain fail-closed and owner-defined
frontiers.safe_pause_condition: execution intent or runtime would be created
frontiers.route_recalculation_trigger: a gate's actual dependency differs from documentation

frontiers.why_sensitive: Provider source paths do not prove credentials, network or deployment reachability.
dissolve_if: separately authorized external evidence is collected
true_hard_if: network or credential authority is required
frontiers.safe_pause_condition: provider or network call would be required
frontiers.route_recalculation_trigger: provider path is removed or contract-gated

frontiers.why_sensitive: Legacy, sandbox, memory and evidence stores have different ownership.
dissolve_if: all writes map to governed destinations
frontiers.safe_pause_condition: write observation or mutation is required
frontiers.route_recalculation_trigger: new destination or store owner appears

frontiers.why_sensitive: Materialization and rollback can cross from sandbox to product state.
dissolve_if: contract tests and static path guards cover the boundary
true_hard_if: product root access cannot be excluded
frontiers.safe_pause_condition: operational root or live store appears

frontiers.why_sensitive: Agent, paper and team definitions can look active without runtime authority.
dissolve_if: all workforce artifacts remain declarative or explicitly gated
true_hard_if: workforce authority or provider activation is requested
frontiers.safe_pause_condition: agent execution or activation is proposed

frontiers.why_sensitive: 3.x closure may require a Direction decision rather than more source inspection.
dissolve_if: Direction accepts the documented exit contract and deferred unknowns
apparent_if: remaining gap is merely documentary drift
true_hard_if: authority, policy or external evidence cannot be delegated

frontier_metrics.not_claimed: This is not a runtime distance, schedule estimate or readiness percentage.

gps_protocol.safe_pause: Freeze product work, preserve green commits, record evidence and do not infer authority.
gps_protocol.route_recalculation_checkpoint: Compare new evidence with destination, phase scope, authority, reversibility and closed work.
gps_protocol.continuation_directive: Resume only with a bounded route that preserves the same destination.
gps_protocol.roadmap_3_2_case: APPARENT_FRONTIER -> SAFE_PAUSE -> ROUTE_RECALCULATION -> CONTINUATION_DIRECTIVE -> SAME_MACRO_MISSION -> PASS -> PUBLICATION
gps_protocol.graph_reordering_rule: Allowed only when same destination, same phase scope, no new authority, reversible/testable and closed work remains valid.
